Definition: a primary particle (enclitic) of connection or addition; both or also (properly, as correlation of G2532):--also, and, both, even, then, whether. Often used in composition, usually as the latter particle.
BiblicalUsage: The word is the little particle and, also, both, that joins things together. Luke writes of all that Jesus began both to do and teach; Paul says the gospel is the power of God unto salvation, to the Jew first, and also to the Greek; and the writer says God also bore witness, both with signs and wonders.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the smallest word does the joining: both to do and teach, Jew and Greek, signs and wonders.
